📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 01:51.

Tottenham Hotspur are keeping tabs on Inter Milan striker Francesco Pio Esposito and Porto centre-forward Samu Omorodion, the latest report has claimed.

The Londoners continued their strong form on Saturday, emerging as 2-0 winners against Ipswich Town, claiming victory for the fourth time in five top-flight games.

Roberto De Zerbi's side are now ninth in the Premier League table with 15 points, and there are hope that the team can push for a European spot.

However, it will be a concern to the head coach that his team have only scored 12 goals in their 11 league fixtures.

It comes as no surprise to see Tottenham linked to both Inter's Esposito and Porto's Omorodion by reputable insider szyexcl on X (formerly Twitter), though they add that it is not clear if they will make a move for either player in January.

Esposito has enjoyed a fine season in Italy with Inter, scoring seven goals and providing one assist in just 767 minutes of football in all competitions.

The 21-year-old has proven himself to be deadly in the penalty area, with all six of his goals in Serie A coming from the middle of the box, though he would arguably be reliant on service from Tottenham's creators.

Omorodion has only played 310 minutes for Porto this season, finding the back of the net twice in that time, but there are concerns about how the 22-year-old would adapt to playing at the highest level in England.

While the striker has often performed well in Portugal, the likes of Darwin Nunez and Viktor Gyokeres struggled to bring their best form over to the Premier League, and it would be understandable if figures at Spurs were wary.

The fact that Tottenham are still in a position where they need significant changes in attack is damning given they spent more than £350m in the summer.

Forwards Omar Marmoush and Savio were both signed, but the former has only scored once in the league this season, while the latter is yet to find the back of the net.

Striker Solanke is the team's leading scorer in the top flight with two goals, though it would be wrong to suggest that he has played well this campaign.

Spurs may be in better form, but if they want to sustain a push for a place in Europe, they must strengthen their forward line.

Jamie Carragher believes that Manchester United face a fight to stay in the Premier League.

The Red Devils remain mired in the top flight’s relegation zone after their heavy 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday, which saw a nightmare debut for fresh manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The Argentine, who began work at Carrington last Wednesday, watched on in horror as his upcoming side were outplayed from the off at Anfield, with Leny Yoro sent off inside eight minutes for hauling down Alexander Isak, who was clean through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz got the goals to round off the rout on Merseyside, and it leaves United with just one win in 12 matches in all competitions.

Recent findings suggest that on Sky Sports, Carragher mentioned: “They’re in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table. You can’t say anything else when you look at their record this season.

According to recent reports, “If the name wasn’t Manchester United and you’re watching the performances, you’d say that is a team that’s in a relegation fight. They’re conceding lots of goals, comedy of errors, red cards, they’ve won one game all season – that is a team in a relegation fight.

In a recent development, “We don’t believe it will happen over a 38-game season but they haven’t had the most difficult of starts. They’ve played a lot of promoted teams, they haven’t played the best team in the league Arsenal yet.

“I don’t think they’ll go down, but this idea that they haven’t got a scrap on their hands- they have.”.

Jamie Carragher believes that Chelsea have “absolutely no chance” of winning silverware with their current crop of central defenders.

The Blues suffered a heavy 4-1 home defeat by Leeds United on Saturday as fans began to turn on Xabi Alonso and his players at Stamford Bridge.

It was a result that leaves them eighth in the Premier League table and five points off the top four.

Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana started in a back four for the west Londoners against their Yorkshire rivals, while summer signing Maxence Lacroix is out injured with a hamstring injury that could keep him out until the turn of the year.

"Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don't change it in January,”Carragher said on Sky Sports.

“They're going to have a significant problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League.

"Colwill at Sunderland against [Brian] Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half time. Fofana's performance against Man United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you'll see from a centre-back this season.

"As a partnership, this will never work because they're not physical enough and there's no real leader there.

"It almost feels like you've got two novices playing, but one cost £75million, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well.".

The former Liverpool defender continued: "Those two can't play in a back four as a two, but it reminds me of myself at Liverpool.

Industry observers note that "We didn't fix it defensively and we were seen as weak, conceding from set pieces and long throws. It wasn't until we signed Sami Hyypia, 6’4”, dominant centre-back, leader, great player, that it changed for us.

"This is not going to change with what they have. Lacroix is a decent player, that's a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim is not a coach who makes a habit of singling out individuals, but he made an exception in Saturday’s press conference.

As MilanNews recall, on the eve of the game against Frosinone, Amorim bluntly admitted that Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot are the ‘irreplaceable’ players in the current squad. Their characteristics and their quality make them unique, in the eyes of the coach and many fans.

When the American and the Frenchman don’t play, the team’s fluidity and effectiveness suffer significantly. There is a stark contract between Milan when Rabiot and Pulisic play versus when both do not feature.

Amorim’s words were clear in his pre-match presser: “Every player appreciates having the club’s trust. And Pulisic’s newly introduced contract has helped. When he wasn’t playing, I told you he was still crucial for Milan, and we can’t forget about the injured players.

It has been revealed that “Pulisic is the only player we can’t replace today: the way he moves between the lines, we don’t have another Pulisic. In the last few European matches, we missed him; we had to manage him. If he’s not on the pitch, given his characteristics, you feel it.

“And you understand how important he is. He doesn’t talk much, but he speaks a lot on the pitch with his play. He always wants the ball. He and Rabiot always lift the team up. I don’t like to talk about individuals, but I have to.

“I think everyone can understand that. So Pulisic is our present, he will be our future, and I think he has the potential to do even more.”.

It’s worth noting that the coach emphasised the importance of Pulisic’s contract renewal too. This is also why the club are doing everything possible to reach an agreement for Rabiot.

In a recent development, cardinale called him a top player and candidly admitted that he adores him, also emphasising how he respects his family. These statements are not coincidental, given that it is his mother who represents the midfielder.

Sources indicate that speaking of which, discussions with Véronique Rabiot are progressing positively. A meeting took place before the derby, which ended with a 3-1 win with a goal for the former Juventus and Marseille midfielder.

The player is happy with the Rossoneri and wants to stay: a definitive agreement on the financial terms needs to be reached. Milan are also willing to adjust the player’s salary in order to secure him for a few more years at Milanello.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

It was a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United, with his 10-man side being thumped 4-0 by old rivals, Liverpool, on Sunday.

And things are not getting any easier during a busy week, which will see him take charge of his first Champions League match in charge, when they travel to Sporting CP.

United's troubles have been well-documented, but they do have six points on the board in the Champions League, meaning they sit just three behind Wednesday's opponents.

Paulo Fonseca has hit the ground running back in his homeland and is looking to help Sporting sneak into the top eight for the second season running.

But will they be able to keep up their perfect start under their new manager, or will Pochettino get United ticking?

Here, using Opta data, we look at the key storylines ahead of the clash at Estadio Jose Alvalade.

This one is almost too close to call, but Sporting just about have the edge.

They won 39.5% of the Opta supercomputer's 10,000 pre-match simulations to United’s 35.7%.

And there is still a healthy 24.8% chance of a draw, though a stalemate would not be the ideal result to boost either side's hopes of automatic qualification.

Sporting and United are meeting for the fifth time and first since the 2007-08 Champions League.

The Portuguese side have won just one of those four prior matches (L3), a 5-0 home victory in March 1964.

But United are unbeaten across their last 13 major European matches against sides from Portugal (W9 D4), since a 2-1 loss to Benfica in the Champions League in December 2005, so they will be hoping to keep that run going.

Fonseca looks to continue perfect start.

Sporting will feel like they have a chance against a wounded United side, especially with three wins from four under their belt in Europe so far in 2026-27.

However, their sole loss did come in their last home game against LASK (2-3).

They are looking to avoid successive home losses in the Champions League for the first time since November 2022, but things do look good, given they have won six of their last eight at Estadio Jose Alvalade in the competition (L2).

But Fonseca will have to overturn recent history if he wants to extend his winning streak to three games, having beaten Moreirense in the Primeira Liga and Serra in the Taca de Portugal.

None of the last five permanent Sporting managers have won their first game in the Champions League, since Paulo Bento in September 2006.

Sporting are by no means the highest scorers in the competition, netting just eight goals so far, while only seven teams have attempted fewer shots than their 46 this term.

Sporting will be hoping to have Luis Suarez back firing as well. He was not on target last time out after scoring in each of their first three outings in Europe this season.

United's defensive woes could cause problems.

There had been a new feeling of hope at Old Trafford following Pochettino's arrival, but the Argentine was given a rude awakening.

United returned from the international break with a thumping 4-0 loss away to old rivals Liverpool, with Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card setting the tone on a difficult day.

They are still struggling in the Premier League – with that loss to Liverpool leaving them 19th in the relegation zone – but there were signs of improvement last time out in Europe.

Despite trailing 2-0 within 17 minutes against Roma, they produced a stunning comeback to snatch a 3-2 win thanks to Matheus Cunha's brace.

The Brazilian is unavailable against Sporting after being sent off shortly after for two bookable offences, and he will be a major miss with only Bruno Fernandes (nine) registering more goal involvements than Cunha in all competitions this term (six – four goals, two assists).

United's troubles in the Champions League have come on the road, though.

In a recent development, they are winless in their last six away games in the competition (D2 L4), losing both this season. They last had a longer such run on their travels between February 2004 and December 2005 (eight matches – D3 L5).

Through the first four matchdays in the Champions League this season, only Slovan Bratislava (293:36) trailed for more minutes than United (263:20).

The Red Devils did win against Roma despite trailing for 76% of the match (73:37), however.

Pochettino's biggest worry will be the defence, with United easily breached four times against Liverpool, though the losing margin could have been much bigger as they rode their luck at times.

No team across the top five European leagues has conceded more goals than United in all competitions (34) this season, while they have conceded at least two goals in each of their last three Champions League games (eight in total).

Never before have they conceded 2+ goals in four consecutive matches in the competition.

Pochettino has a huge task on his hands to turn things around at United, but a win would take them level on points with 10th-place Sporting, and would keep their outside chances of an automatic spot alive.

Rui Silva possesses an 85.7% save percentage in the Champions League – currently the best percentage in the competition.

While Silva has only played two Champions League games so far, he has conceded only once (a Goncalo Inacio own goal against Galatasaray).

He has faced seven shots on target in total, making six saves, while he has prevented 0.8 goals according to Opta's expected goals on target model (xGoT).

Manchester United – Bruno Fernandes.

With his penalty against Roma, Fernandes netted his 24th goal in major European competition for United, moving ahead of Cristiano Ronaldo into seventh spot on the club's all-time scoring list.

Only Ruud van Nistelrooy (five) has scored more penalties for United in the Champions League than Fernandes (four – level with Wayne Rooney).

Across all competitions, only Pascal Gross (59) has created more chances among Premier League players than the United captain (43), who has nine goal involvements in total in 2026-27 (six goals, three assists).

Manchester City could bring Enzo Fernandez back into their starting XI on Tuesday, when they face Napoli in the Champions League.

The midfielder started on the bench when the Citizens faced Fulham on Saturday, with the Argentine having received criticism for his poor defensive displays.

However, it may be unrealistic to expect teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi to start once again, so perhaps Fernandez will partner Elliot Anderson in a double pivot.

Antoine Semenyo's knee injury will keep him out of Tuesday's clash, meaning fans are likely to see Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku stationed out wide in attack.

Rayan Cherki is set to come back into the team in favour of Phil Foden, and the Frenchman will be tasked with supporting striker Erling Haaland.

Should right-back Matheus Nunes miss out, it would not be surprising to see Enzo Maresca play Abdukodir Khusanov on that side of the backline.

Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol are candidates to start in the other three positions in defence, while goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma can be pencilled into the lineup.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sixth-placed City, who drew 2-2 with struggling Doncaster Rovers at the weekend, face another White Rose side who have had a difficult autumn in the Reds, who find themselves at the bottom of League One following Bromley's weekend win at Reading.

Without a win in 10 league games since September 2 and in their worst league position for many a year, the Oakwell outfit look like being in the thick of a survival fight for the rest of the season and face the very real prospect of fourth-tier football next term for the first time since 1978-79 if their fortunes don't turn around in the fresh year.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It's a far cry from their highs in their one season under Duff in 2022-23 when they reached the play-off final and went desperately close to promotion back to the Championship.

Duff, who was at Oakwell to watch his old club take on Sheffield Wednesday on Friday - the hosts lost 2-1, the margin of defeat for their past five league losses - remarked: "Barnsley didn't look like a wounded animal on Friday, but a football team with loads of energy and good players.

According to recent reports, "I don't think we're at a point now where we can assume that, well: 'we're just better than them'. Everything that's got us, this football club, the team, the squad, to where it has and the success it's had, is because it's had that underdog mentality. What we can't have is we slip into 'oh, we're better than them'.. Because that's when trouble starts, isn't it?

"I watched them on Friday against Sheffield Wednesday and they should have got some out of the game.

"Barnsley found themselves 2-0 down and then were really, really good for the rest of the game.

"It's not like the Premier League where you very rarely see teams at the bottom of the league beat the teams at the top. In this league, it happens all the time.

“Bromley have beaten Reading, Peterborough have beaten Plymouth. It's not a league where you (think) we’ll beat them or ‘two home games, we’ll win them’.

"Our lads' mentality and attitude is pretty good. I don't think we have that sort of arrogance in terms of ‘we'll be alright, we'll just win today.’.

"They know what they have to do, they know the effort they have to put in, the application, the energy they have to put into every game and since I've been here they've done that every game.

"They did it before we came and, like I remarked, they just nicked a couple early in the season. We've done enough where we should have won them and we haven't quite nicked them.".

Sources indicate that city are on a run of nine matches in just under a month in four different competitions and they face midweek games for the next four matches. Tonight is also their final game of a six-match run of fixtures at Valley Parade.

Duff continued: "There are games that are coming now.

"There’s no way there is going to be the same 11 players on Tuesday or the following Saturday or the following Tuesday or the following Saturday.

"We’ll wrap a few up that we need to and there will be opportunities for people.

Industry observers note that "The good thing with competition is they know they’ll get opportunities so they need to be ready. If you get given a chance and you don’t take it, it might not come around again so swiftly.

"That’s when the training of the lads who aren’t in the team is so crucial, the lifestyle, the commitment to the job, the commitment to the team.

"Don’t be the one that’s caught out partying or eating junk food because you’re not letting yourself down, you’re letting your teammates down. But I don’t think we need to worry about any of that in this group.".

Paul Merson has questioned Chelsea’s decision to appoint Xabi Alonso in the summer.

The Blues sank to a new low over the weekend when they were thrashed 4-1 by Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

It saw the west Londoners slump to eighth in the Premier League table, five points off the top four.

They have now registered just one win in their last five games as pressure piles on Alonso in his first term in the hotseat.

On Sky Sports, Merson, the former Arsenal striker, disputed the Spaniard’s appointment and rhetorically asked why Liverpool had not hired their former midfielder, despite him being a free agent and Arne Slot being sacked at the end of the season.

"My biggest worry is that Liverpool could have had Alonso and they chose not to,” he remarked.

“Obviously, Liverpool didn't think he was good enough.

It has been revealed that "Alonso took the Chelsea job, and Liverpool sacked Slot two weeks later. You can't tell me that Liverpool couldn't have spoken to Alonso and say: 'Don't take the Chelsea job, we're going to take you'.

Recent findings suggest that "He was out of a job as well, Liverpool could have had him and he'd have gone there all day long. So why didn't they take him? Did they know something that we're seeing now?

"It just always sits in my mind. That was my worry - and now it's playing out.”.

Merson compared Alonso to his predecessor, Liam Rosenior, who was dismissed after just three months in charge, having lost five consecutive league games without scoring - the club’s first time since 1912.

"If this was Rosenior in charge at Chelsea and getting these results, he'd be in major trouble,” Merson continued.

In a recent development, “100 per cent, he'd be in trouble. And remember, Rosenior didn't have Morgan Rogers in his team, bought for £116million.

"But it's because of the unbelievable job [Alonso] did at Bayer Leverkusen that everybody is thinking: ‘It will be alright.".

So it should come as no surprise that his Bradford City career has started to find a bit of momentum since Duff moved to Valley Parade.

Having come close a number of times, Phillips scored his first Bantams goal at home to Peterborough United at the end of October, and added two more and an assist against Marine in the FA Cup.

Being reunited with Michael Duff is bringing more out of the 28-year-old, hampered by injury in the early part of the season. He is determined to repay the manager’s faith.

"Working with a manager before always helps, especially for me because I probably had one of my best seasons there," says Phillips, part of the Barnsley team which took Sheffield Wednesday to extra-time in the 2023 League One play-off final.

“He puts an arm around me and gives me that confidence to go out and create chances and score goals.

“But he's also on me for getting fit and doing lots of running. So I need to keep working hard. He puts trust in me, so I need to pay him back.”.

It was not damaged by the fact in that 2023 Wembley final Phillips’s red card left Barnsley playing the majority of Duff’s final game in charge with ten men.

“There was just a little bit of banter (when Duff spoke to him for the first time since, having just taken over at Valley Parade) because I got sent off the last time I played under him," states Phillips. "But he got his move to Swansea anyway, so it was all good.”.

Duff was brought in as a "continuity" candidate because of his perceived similarities to Graham Alexander when his old Burnley team-mate left to manage Preston North End in September.

“He's not changed a lot, really," says Phillips. "He's implemented some of his idea but we're still getting results and doing a lot of the right things.

“He’s not just going to come in and rip it all up.

“But I think slowly he might add a few little things that he wants to do, which is fine, and the lads will get time to work on it on the training pitch.

“The lads are buying into it and you can see it on the pitch.”.

After a good start to the season, Phillips believes Duff can go one better than he did with Barnsley in League One. Following four league games without a win, the pressure will be on to take one at home to the bottom-of-the-table Reds.

“What the club achieved last year was really special, having just come up from League Two," states Phillips.

Sources indicate that “But the ambition this year is to be near the top and be fighting for promotion. We've got a great squad with a lot of talented players and we've started off really well.

“For the lads, it's just keeping the feet on the ground and taking each game as it comes.

“The fans always get excited and they can have their opinion but as a team and as a squad, we just keep ticking away and getting results and putting points on the board.”.

"Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that but it takes some time.".

"You go there and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn't give you any advantage, so you need to earn it.

"Ethan has, first of all, the mindset to do it and then the quality to do it and these things are part of a journey and part of a season and he needs to reveal himself and earn the right to win.".

The callowness of the Reds has been exposed at times this season but as part of a young Northern Ireland team which has had an exceptional start to the season, winning promotion to the top division of the Nations League, Kelly is loathe to use that as an excuse.

It has been revealed that "The Northern Ireland team is young, but it's a really experienced team," stressed former Doncaster Rovers player Kelly. "I think if you look at the amount of caps some of the lads have, the Charles brothers (former Sheffield Wednesday players Shea and Pierce) are 23 and 21, but they've played (a combined 57) international games.

"Here it's a lot of lads' first seasons in the EFL, which is completely different.

"But I think young players are fearless and we probably do need to stop looking at us as a young team.

Sources indicate that "I don't actually think that's the reason why we're losing so many games. It's nothing to do with that, I think.".

Whilst the age of the squad probably is a bigger factor than Kelly will admit, he is right that there is no point falling back on it as that will not change this side of the January transfer window at the very earliest.

What Barnsley’s strategy is meant to do is accelerate the development of young players, and Kelly feels wearing the captain's armband – or even taking on more responsibility when others do – is enhancing his game.

"I really enjoy it," he remarked. "It was a bit different for me coming back this season. From the very start, it was just a lot of a younger changing room.

"I felt really older when I came back compared to when I joined here last year. But it'll be really good for me in the future. I'm quite enjoying it.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm looking up to Carm a lot, the captain of the group. I speak with him nearly every day. He's really helping me.".

But the focus just has to be on securing a first win in 11 league games.

Sources indicate that "We've got a chance to try and bounce back," noted Kelly. "We need to start winning games, so hopefully start on Tuesday.

"It will be another big crowd, with a good atmosphere.

In a recent development, "It just makes everyone play another five to ten per cent better, run a bit more when there's a big crowd. I think the big atmospheres do help.

"Hopefully, it'll help us track a win on Tuesday.".

Daniel Stendel has a decision to make at right-back after Jubril Okedina – a central defender playing out of position there – was culpable for goals in the last two matches.

“It’s a little bit like our performance," said the coach. "We played well but in little moments we are not ready and conceded the goal. He is similar.

Industry observers note that "It was not only his fault but he was the last player and maybe he can defend this ball better. It was team mistakes.

“We have the chance to do it better at Bradford and we have some ideas to change some things in the first 11, maybe not.”.

After four games out of the XI, Tyrese Noslin is an option.

Recent findings suggest that "I think a little bit in the first games it’s not his quality in possession that he has to improve, it’s more his physical game out of possession," said Stendel. "He tried to adapt his game so much more in training every week.

"I hope maybe on Tuesday or maybe Saturday he is ready to start and show he does the next step in his career.".

Vitaly Janelt scored a 30-yard screamer as Brentford romped to a 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

One win in five had seen some of the early season optimism around Keith Andrews’ team fade but this was an emphatic response to fire them up the Premier League table to sixth, even if culpability for Everton’s collapse lay largely with James Tarkowski, red carded in the 40th minute for a horror tackle on Yehor Yarmolyuk.

David Moyes was setting a fresh record for number of games in charge, this his 593rd match eclipsing the tally of Harry Catterick racked up during the 60s and 70s, but this was a terrible first half and was no way to mark such an achievement.

According to recent reports, everything went wrong for the visitors. Both Brentford goals scored by Keane Lewis-Potter came via deflections and Tarkowski’s momentary abdication of responsibility as captain, lunging studs-up into the shin of Yarmolyuk with his team 2-0 down, would have been impossible for Moyes to mitigate. He was let down badly by one of his senior players in a moment of direst need.

Industry observers note that thereafter the game was little contest. It might have trickled towards a routine two-goal win for Brentford had Janelt not pulled out a brilliant strike from range that ripped past Jordan Pickford to rub salt in the wound for Moyes, and for Tarkowski.

Fabio Carvalho bundled one in from on the goal-line with his knee in stoppage time, the final indignity for Everton.

Brentford were excellent throughout. Early on, Callum Wilson fed Michael Kayode arriving up on the right, the full-back given a clear shot on Pickford’s goal but dragged his effort badly across the face and wide.

It has been revealed that everton were making it too easy. Midway through the half they failed to deal with a ball over the top and Jaidon Anthony sent it low into the middle with a deft stab of the toe. It was a beautifully controlled first-time pass, finding Lewis-Potter arriving in an acre of space and his shot spun in off the lunging Jarrad Branthwaite.

It took less than two minutes for Lewis-Potter to hit a near-identical second, with a ball into the box from Mikkel Damsgaard met with unconvincing Everton defending.

The Brentford midfielder was given two attempts, his first shot rebounding back to him to squeeze the ball in at the second go via a deflection off Thierno Barry.

In a recent development, everton were sinking and their captain abandoned them to their fate. Tarkowski was first shown only a yellow for a studs-up challenge on Yarmolyuk. A single look at a replay confirmed the foul was far more serious, the defender’s boot connecting high on the shin of Yarmolyuk’s standing leg and his dismissal was inevitable.

Tech Report: Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.
  • After just eight minutes, his aims were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his aims were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he said, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

Sources indicate that 'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

And his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

The Reds were rampant at Anfield last weekend, thrashing their fierce rivals to spoil Mauricio Pochettino’s bow as the Red Devils’ new boss.

Dutch midfielder Gravenberch was forced to sit out with a persistent heel fracture, but manager Andoni Iraola has mentioned that the injury is a “day by day” situatiuon.

Fellow Netherlands international Cody Gakpo was also sidelined for the visit of United with a calf problem that he picked up on international duty, and he is set to miss out again here for the trip to Belgium, when the Merseysiders take on Club Brugge in the Champions League.

Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk were welcome returners from their respective injury scares, while Rio Ngumoha played a starring role in the demolition job on Sunday in place of Gakpo off the left flank.

You would expect Iraola to plump for a similar side, with Ronald Araujo at right-back, Jeremy Jacquet partnering Van Dijk and Milos Kerkez completing the back four ahead of Alisson.

In the engine room, Alexis Mac Allister was joined by Dominik Szoboszlai, who himself had been an injury concern, and that should be the partnership once more unless Gravenberch returns or Trey Nyoni is given an opportunity.

Ahead of them, Florian Wirtz’s good form continued as he registered a goal in the thrashing, and he was flanked by the dangerous Ngumoha and summer signing Bradley Barcola.

Alexander Isak led the line by example on Sunday, and should get the nod once more, with Hugo Ekitike still out with his Achilles rupture.

There could be returns to the squad for defenders Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley, with the pair finally making their comebacks to training after their serious knee injuries.

He told The Yorkshire Post: “[I am] very pleased because Brenden had perhaps a period when he was not playing with this clarity in this game, and for that he had to wait a few games for his chance.

“Sean Longstaff has chipped in, after he had not too many minutes in the beginning of the season, right now also really excellent performances.

“Harry Wilson today again with another key pass, also before the goal, so it's important that he makes an impact.”.

After Leeds’ win over Tottenham Hotspur prior to the international break, Melvin Bard’s impact from the bench featured prominently in post-match discussions.

Farke’s leading lights tend to hog the headlines, yet the German is keen for every member of the squad to believe they can have an impact.

Bogle has made no secret of his desire to break into the England squad, but faces stiff competition from high-profile stars.

“You just don't get into the England team now,” Hateley told The Yorkshire Post. “We have a lot of good players.

In a recent development, “You just have to look at the World Cup, some of the players that didn't go to the World Cup. We are where we are. We've got a Ballon d'Or winner, Harry Kane.

Two of his Leeds teammates - James Trafford and Dominic Calvert-Lewin - were named in Thomas Tuchel’s last England squad.

Wesley Fofana has revealed he almost quit football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge of Chelsea.

The French centre-back claims he considered retiring early due to the psychological strain that came with a rash of injuries.

Fofana, 25, did continue playing and is starting regularly this season for Chelsea, but has been much criticised in recent weeks for his performances under Xabi Alonso, including in Saturday’s 4-1 home defeat to Leeds.

“There was a period when I was recovering from my cruciate ligament and meniscus injuries,” Fofana said.

Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

After Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in October against Barcelona, Desire Doue went down with the same injury against Nice on the weekend.

Both forwards have been ruled out for the remainder of 2026-27, placing more impetus on the likes of Mika Godts, Maghnes Akliouche and Ferran Torres.

PSG did receive a boost ahead of their Champions League encounter with Roma on Wednesday, with Ousmane Dembele making his return from injury against Nice.

Luis Enrique believes his attacking players now have an opportunity to showcase their talents after the injuries to Kvaratskhelia and Doue.

In a recent development, "I feel sad for the players, but it's a wonderful opportunity to show our level. It's a great challenge to take on," said the Spaniard.

Sources indicate that "This is normal. All teams have injured players. In this case, it's not normal to have injuries as serious as those of Kvara and Des'. We remain focused on the players' recovery.".

"This team have shown their ability to be resilient; it's a great challenge to take on, to think about improving, to find solutions, whether in the tactical or technical aspect.".

However, they will need to keep a close eye on Donyell Malen, who has been directly involved in six goals in the Champions League this season (four goals, two assists).

The only Roma player with more goal involvements in a single edition is Edin Dzeko (10 in 2017-18 and eight in 2018-19).

"We all know the AS Roma players, especially the forwards. Malen used to play on the wing, and when he moved into the centre, he indicated his ability to score goals," added Luis Enrique.

"His goal tally is incredible. We'll have to be careful with the forwards, but also with all the players, because mobility is important for Roma.

AC Milan and Adidas will be back together again from 2028, and the German brand want to launch the fresh era with a bi bang.

Sources indicate that as Calciomercato.com write, Milan will return to being an Adidas club again, as they have been for three previous spells. The two brands became so closely linked above all by the successes of the 2000s under Carlo Ancelotti, before PUMA took over in 2018.

The contract with Adidas – which will begin in the summer of 2028 – is quite a sensational deal for the industry and for the club’s final years in terms of sporting results. It will bring in €50m per season for 10 seasons, the highest in Serie A by some margin.

Ten years ago, the Rossoneri signed a €14m per season contract with PUMA, which was renewed in 2022 to reach around €25m per season.

In a recent development, adidas have already invested heavily in Milan and they want to strengthen the ‘alliance’ further. A lot depends on building a squad capable of playing a leading role in both Serie A and the Champions League.

It has been revealed that for this reason, Adidas are hoping to help Milan land a world-class player. Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay could gain momentum in the coming months as an idea, as the former Manchester United player is one of Adidas’s most important players worldwide.

Industry observers note that bruno Fernandes is another name to keep an eye on. The Manchester United captain left Italy many years ago as a promising youngster and now wants to return as a top player. The Portuguese is a possible candidate, even if he is right now twinned with Nike.

Last but not least – in terms of consideration and feasibility – is Real Madrid’s Endrick. Milan are ready to make him one of the symbols of their new project and have a bid of €60m plus bonuses ready to try to break down Los Blancos’ wall.

Industry observers note that jose Mourinho is the main obstacle between the Rossoneri and the Brazilian star, but Cardinale is unwavering and ready to do everything possible to bring him to Milanello as early as January. The money from Adidas could help land Endrick, who is with New Balance at present.

Despite a budget that remains tight, the Catalan hierarchy should nevertheless be active in January and three targets appear to stand out, Mundo Deportivo explained midweek.

Whether he has changed his mind to the point of agreeing to the signing of the Inter player is far from certain.

According to the same source, the 61-year-old manager also reportedly vetoed the arrival of two other players: Aymeric Laporte and Cristian Romero.

Industry observers note that the name of the France-born Spain international was reportedly set aside because the club did not want to base a decision solely on his level during the World Cup and apparently had doubts about his ability to maintain that form over the long term. The Argentine, for his part, did not win Flick's favour because he is not left-footed.

It has been revealed that the journalist adds that the German's ideal profile is Josko Gvardiol, but a deal for him was too difficult to complete. The problem will probably be the same in January with the Croatia international.

One thing is certain given Mundo Deportivo's revelations: Hansi Flick apparently has the final say on a large share of potential signings.

That he did could be huge for the Tigers' hopes of staying in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that being able to bury disappointment is key for any player who plays at the level Tzolakis does, but especially goalkeepers. Of course, being a Hull player, he had a joke from his always-upbeat coach Sergej Jakirovic to help him through the process.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Even the finest goalkeepers have bad days and sometimes they are not even their fault.

Despite being one of the best stoppers in this season's Premier League, the £20m signing from Olympiacos has been questioned over a couple of the goals he has conceded in the early stages of his Hull career, such is the life of a goalkeeper.

Apart from the largely irrelevant sixth, Tzolakis was fairly blameless as Greece lost 7-0 in the Netherlands during the last international break.

Even so, he was taken out of the firing line for the final Nations League group game, where Greece needed a goal difference miracle to qualify for the knockout stages.

But in his next game, for Hull at home to in-form Brighton and Hove Albion, he was outstanding, making a string of key saves in the first half without which, two-goal Oli McBurnie would never have been able to secure their first win since August in stoppage-time.

It spoke wonders for the character of the 24-year-old, who has the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in this season's top flight.

"If you don't keep content and forget it, it's more difficult to survive in this Premier League," reflected Tzolakis after the 2-0 win.

"It was a bad day for our team (in Amsterdam). We didn't play well and it's easy after one, two, three goals to concede more goals. Three days later the Netherlands conceded five goals against Germany.

"But the most notable thing is to forget this and to continue.".

Sources indicate that jakirovic has been there and got the T-shirt having lost his only Champions League game so far as a coach – and his last match for Dinamo Zagreb, as it swiftly turned out. So he knows how to deal with disappointment.

Sources indicate that "We spoke about it just through jokes, because I know how it is," noted the 49-year-old. "I lost 9-2 one time against Bayern Munich, it was like we played on a PlayStation.

Industry observers note that "You can't do anything (about it), like England-Croatia 7-0, you can't do anything, you can put on substitutions, fresh blood, upcoming energy, no way (will it change things). You lost the game and that's it.

"You just have to keep going, go forward and ciao. You cannot change anything, it's the past.".

And Hull's win was massive for their confidence.

They might have gone into the game as the highest-ranked of this season's newly-promoted sides, and they might have kept above the psychologically-important point-per-game mark, but their last win was starting to feel a long way away, at Coventry City on the second weekend of the season.

In a recent development, "The feeling is great for us," said Tzolakis. "After Coventry, we also had some good games but we didn't take three points.

Industry observers note that "It was a very good performance for our team. We suffered in the first half, but we achieved two goals in the last minutes, so we took the three points.

"I enjoyed it a lot because I helped my team to achieve the target for the day.

"tI's very good when you have a very good performance, to have someone to score a goal and to take the three points.

"It was a huge victory against a very good team like Brighton, but we have to continue because we have a lot of games and we have to survive in the league.

In a recent development, "It's my job to keep my team in the game. We suffered a lot in the first half, but I think in the second half we managed the game better.

"We had some chances before the red card (for Brighton’s Joao Costinha), but after the red card it was easier for us to score.

"Every single point is too key for the Premier League, but if we score a goal and we take three points, it's much better than one point.".

And if the win was a boost to Tzolakis' confidence, the same was true of McBurnie, who scored a penalty and a free-kick to break his duck for the season at the end of October, before adding two six-yard box finishes against the Seagulls.

According to recent reports, "He's doing a lot," said Jakirovic. "On Sunday he played against (Luka) Vuskovic, who is a Croatian star, excellent young player, (born in) 2007.

"Oli was good, the fight was there, excellent, and I'm very happy for him because finally he scored from open play.

Sources indicate that "I don't have any doubt about Oli McBurnie because he's a natural leader. He doesn't need (the armband), he's leading his team together with (Regan) Slater, with Coyley (Lewie Coyle), with Crooksy (Matt Crooks). They are very vital.

"John Egan is also very notable for us.".

Bruno Fernandes laid into the standard of Premier League referees after Manchester United were beaten by Liverpool at the weekend.

The Red Devils played most of the match with ten men after Leny Yoro was dismissed for tripping Alexander Isak, who was through on goal, and Dominik Szoboszlai powered home the opener from the resultant free kick.

Fernandes, whose future remains up in the air with his current contract due to expire in the summer, played the full duration at Anfield and cut a frustrated figure at the full-time whistle.

Speaking post-match, he questioned referee Sam Barrott’s decision to dismiss Yoro. Several pundits have questioned whether Isak’s heavy touch had killed his chances of scoring from the one-on-one, with debate raging for days post-match.

“I’m not complaining,” Fernandes caveated, speaking in Portuguese to ESPN Brasil. “The situation is clear from what they explain to us at the start of the season.

“I think we have far too many meetings with referees for them to explain the rules, only for the referees themselves not to know them.

Recent findings suggest that “We have four officials at the game, plus another two on VAR. I understand it’s a difficult situation, but VAR can watch it again and again, with replays, slow motion, everything.

Sources indicate that “Isak puts his leg in front of Leny simply to try to win a foul. The ball is knocked forward, towards Senne’s hands. He has absolutely no control of the ball.

“For me, fine, it’s a foul. But you can’t send him off because there’s no control of the ball. It’s not a situation where Isak is going one-on-one with the goalkeeper. So I think the punishment was a bit harsh on Leny.”.

Wesley Fofana has revealed he almost quit football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge of Chelsea.

The French centre-back indicates he considered retiring early due to the psychological strain that came with a rash of injuries.

Fofana, 25, did continue playing and is starting regularly this season for Chelsea, but has been much criticised in recent weeks for his performances under Xabi Alonso, including in Saturday’s 4-1 home defeat to Leeds.

“There was a period when I was recovering from my cruciate ligament and meniscus injuries,” Fofana stated.

“Then I suffered two consecutive hamstring strains under Enzo Maresca, when I really decided: ‘That’s it, I’m retiring, I’m done playing.’ I was serious.

“I really wanted to stop, because, for the first time in my life, I wasn’t happy anymore. It wasn’t just about being injured or not playing; my whole life was completely shattered. I wasn’t myself anymore. I sincerely believed that, in the future, I would only get injured.

“I thought to myself: ‘That’s it, football isn’t for me, I’m too fragile.’ I even used Abou Diaby as an example. I thought to myself: ’I guess I’m the Abou Diaby of our generation. There has to be someone like that, and it happened to me. It’s my destiny, I accept it.’”.

It has been revealed that fofana, speaking in an interview with Zack Nani TV, continued: “Of course, I was very sad and didn’t want to stop, because I was living my dream. At that point, I called my agents so we could sit down and talk, telling them, ‘Okay, I’ve decided to retire.’.

In a recent development, “They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that: ‘It’s simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there’s a lot of money to be made. Even if you really decide to stop playing, you still have to come every day, keep smiling, and even if you’re injured, you have to honour your contract for your future.’.

“But at that moment, I really felt that the pain football caused me far outweighed the joy, so why continue? I was in pain almost 100 per cent of the time. Every time I gritted my teeth, played a few games, and just started to find a little love and joy in life again, bang, I’d get injured again.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:35.

Mikel Arteta's concern over David Raya has grown beyond the result of the 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday. The Spanish goalkeeper had to leave the pitch in the second half following a collision with William Osula, and has become a source of apprehension at Arsenal.

Still without a definitive diagnosis, the player is due to undergo tests to determine the severity of the problem, but the possibility of missing a few weeks represents a significant setback for Arsenal's plans.

In a recent development, raya received treatment on the pitch, but continued to show discomfort and was unable to remain in the match. Kepa Arrizabalaga came on in his place, 25 minutes into the second half. In his post-match interview, Arteta did not hide his concern over the situation of his first-choice goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that 'Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. Tomorrow, he will have an MRI scan, but at the moment I do not know' - the manager mentioned.

The apprehension is understandable. Raya is not just Arsenal's first-choice goalkeeper: he has become a central piece in the way the team organise themselves defensively and start their moves. His security when coming off his line, ability to play with his feet and involvement in build-up from the back make him a reference point within Arteta's model. Finding a replacement capable of reproducing all of these characteristics is no simple task.

Arteta's first alternative is set. Signed to join the squad and provide depth in the position, Kepa is Raya's immediate understudy and took over as soon as the Spaniard had to leave the pitch against Newcastle.

Should the injury rule the first-choice goalkeeper out for a few weeks, the former Real Madrid man will have the opportunity to show that he can sustain the team's competitive level at an important point in the season.

Recent findings suggest that the question, however, involves more than simply filling the spot. Kepa has experience at substantial clubs and knows the demands of playing decisive matches, but his record also includes episodes that fuel doubts about his consistency. His performance against Newcastle, for example, was not enough to remove the question marks over his ability to take over as first choice without Arsenal suffering a drop in performance.

In a recent development, the most uncomfortable memory for supporters is the League Cup final last season against Manchester City. On that occasion, a mistake by Kepa carried weight in the result and reinforced the criticism of the goalkeeper.

While an isolated episode does not determine a player's ability, the current situation demands that he offer answers on the pitch, especially if he has to take over the position for a longer period.

Industry observers note that the challenge also lies in the differences between the styles of the two Spaniards. Raya offers a combination of reflexes, positioning and quality in distribution that allows Arsenal to maintain their approach even when under opposition pressure. Kepa will need to show security both in his interventions and in his decisions with the ball, preventing the change in goal from causing significant alterations to the defensive functioning.

According to recent reports, in addition to Kepa, Arsenal have Illan Meslier in the squad. The Frenchman appears as another possibility for Arteta, although he is behind the Spaniard in the goalkeeping hierarchy.

His presence widens the options available, but does not necessarily mean the manager is willing to promote an immediate change in the order of preference.

Giving Meslier an opportunity would be a decision involving risks and benefits. On the one hand, it would allow Arsenal to assess an alternative in a position that may require more than one player over the course of the season.

On the other, backing a goalkeeper who does not right now occupy the first position in the contest could represent an even bigger change in a system that would already need to adapt to Raya's absence.

The possibility of looking for a reinforcement in the January transfer window may also enter the debate, particularly if the tests confirm a more serious injury and a lengthy recovery period. Even so, signing another goalkeeper would not be an automatic solution. Besides market availability, Arsenal would need to find a player who offered the conditions to take over as first choice and adapt rapidly to Arteta's demands.

Recent findings suggest that the timing of the season makes the situation even more delicate. Arsenal lead the Premier League and also have important commitments in the Champions League. In the coming weeks, the team will face opponents such as Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham and Real Madrid, a sequence that will demand concentration and consistency in every area.

How the Dylan Tombides Foundation is educating footballers about testicular cancer

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that 15 years ago, a random drugs test at the Under-17 World Cup revealed that West Ham striker and Australian youth international Dylan Tombides had testicular cancer.
  • Originally misdiagnosed by his GP as a cyst, Tombides’ mother, Tracy, and brother, Taylor, are now on a mission to minimise the likelihood of such a mistake happening again by getting people to know what to look for.
  • Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in males aged 15 to 44, but highly treatable and in most cases curable when detected early - so education is key to saving lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that 15 years ago, a random drugs test at the Under-17 World Cup revealed that West Ham striker and Australian youth international Dylan Tombides had testicular cancer. He would pass away three years later at the age of 20.

Originally misdiagnosed by his GP as a cyst, Tombides’ mother, Tracy, and brother, Taylor, are now on a mission to minimise the likelihood of such a mistake happening again by getting people to know what to look for.

Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in males aged 15 to 44, but highly treatable and in most cases curable when detected early - so education is key to saving lives.

That is why the DT38 Foundation was set up in Dylan’s name and why Tracy and Taylor, in partnership with FIFA Medical, are explaining to players at this year’s U17 World Cup in Doha why regular self-examination matters and how to carry it out.

“Getting the call from FIFA was a massive opportunity and an amazing thing for us and for the charity,” Taylor tells Standard Sport.

Sources indicate that “Obviously, it’s where Dylan last kind of played healthy before his diagnosis. So to come back to where it all started for us as a family is a grateful honour.”.

£75m Chelsea star ‘considered retirement’ under Maresca.

Fernandes fumes in unseen interview amid fresh Man Utd red card verdict.

Chelsea injury update: Caicedo, Joao Pedro, James latest return dates.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

Tracy and Taylor have spoken to more than 1,200 players across the tournament, and their story has really hit home.

“One of the young players stood in front of me and mentioned, ‘I’m so sorry for your loss. I’m sorry your son isn’t coming home to you. We are so grateful that you are telling us all about it’,” Tracy says.

“(We are) very grateful to have this opportunity to educate 1,200 players out here this fortnight, that hopefully will go home and pass on the message of the signs and symptoms of testicular cancer and the importance of an ultrasound scan.”.

The DT38 foundation have a campaign called ‘Check One Two’, encouraging men to check themselves on the first day of every month.

Dylan’s nickname - ‘Didge’ - also provides an acronym and hashtag for the foundation: Delay Is Deadly, Get Educated.

FIFA medical director Andy Massey has worked with the DT38 Foundation to get Tracy and Taylor talking to players at the U17 World Cup and claims it is an initiative that he hopes to continue year on year.

“What I would love to do is carry this on next year for the Under-17s,” Massey claims.

Industry observers note that “It’s an annual event now (the World Cup) for Under-17s. We’re going to be in the same place until 2029, and it would be fantastic to do it (talk to players) again for next year and the year after.”.

We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it.

Massey continued by underlining the value of the work Tracy and Taylor are doing, with free scans now on offer to players during the tournament.

“We don’t want this to be a box-ticking exercise. We don’t want this to be a, ‘Let’s pat ourselves on the back, we’re working for a charity’.

“This is one of the biggest things that I think I’ve ever done in my sports medicine career because it has such a reach.”.

The DT38 Foundation are starting with the U17 World Cup, but ultimately Taylor hopes their work will have an impact down the generations.

Industry observers note that “The effect is lasting,” he states. “If we can teach these kids now, we know the next generation, they’ll teach their kids and they’ll teach their kids and it’ll be continuous.

Industry observers note that “We’re not just affecting one life, we’re affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it. Without FIFA, we couldn’t touch as many people as we have.”.

Visit dt38.org to find out more about the DT38 Foundation, Dylan's story and advice and guidance about testicular cancer.

  • PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday at the Allianz Riviera, in round 11 of Ligue 1, brought terrible news for Luis Enrique.
  • Shortly before half-time, Desire Doue, who had scored a goal minutes earlier, collapsed to the ground after twisting his right knee while attempting a dribble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:48.

PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday at the Allianz Riviera, in round 11 of Ligue 1, brought terrible news for Luis Enrique.

Shortly before half-time, Desire Doue, who had scored a goal minutes earlier, collapsed to the ground after twisting his right knee while attempting a dribble. Amid cries of pain, the winger had to leave the pitch on a stretcher when substituted.

Speaking to Ligue 1+, the Spanish manager said in advance that Doue's injury 'was serious', a fear confirmed on Sunday. Imaging results found that the PSG number 14 has suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament and will have to undergo surgery in the coming days.

Sources indicate that PSG have not disclosed a recovery timeline, but cases similar to Desire Doue's that require surgical intervention show that players usually spend at least six months in the medical department. The 21-year-old Frenchman should therefore only return to action at the end of May.

According to recent reports, in the most optimistic scenario, Doue would be fit in time for a possible Champions League final, to be played on 5 June at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Spain. However, depending on the strategy PSG adopt to cover for the young winger's absence, the success of this season is at risk.

Signed in August 2024 from Rennes for £42.5m (€50m), Desire Doue became one of Luis Enrique's trusted men, so much so that he was an crucial part of the rotation in his debut season (16 goals and 14 assists in 61 matches) and was named man of the match in the European final against Inter Milan, when he scored twice.

According to recent reports, in 2025-26, the French attacking midfielder had his run at PSG interrupted by two muscle injuries, but still managed 13 goals and eight assists in 40 matches, as well as scoring his penalty as PSG won back-to-back Champions League titles against Arsenal. And after representing his country at the World Cup, Doue was enjoying an overwhelming start to the season.

As a reward for his good form at PSG, Doue began to gain more space in the France team under Zinedine Zidane, who even said that he reminded him of himself when he played as a midfielder, because of his personality of always wanting to improve by listening to older players.

More than the impact in the final third, Doue is also a joker for the PSG manager because of his two-footedness, able to play on either wing.

The Frenchman had been playing on the left in recent weeks as a replacement for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who also suffered an anterior cruciate ligament rupture in his right knee during the win over Barcelona on 20 October, in the Champions League.

Industry observers note that the Georgian underwent surgery and should only be available to the Spanish manager in mid-April. With two heavyweight absences in the attacking system, PSG must ask themselves whether it is necessary to reinforce the area when the transfer window reopens, or whether the current squad will be enough to remain competitive on all fronts.

If PSG conclude that the solution lies in the market, they will have to do very meticulous work to find someone who fits Luis Enrique's playing philosophy, based on high intensity and constant movement, and who is available to leave in January. It is true that there is no shortage of talents around the world who fit those requirements, but the certainty is that no signing would be cheap, nor a guarantee of immediate success.

On the other hand, if PSG give a vote of confidence to the current players, which at the moment is the public discourse, they will have to get more out of their players. 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele has suffered from different physical problems in 2026-27, so much so that he has constantly been placed on a load management regime.

Ferran Torres, signed from Barcelona for £42.5m (€50m), had an exciting start at PSG, with seven goals in the first six matches. However, as in his Camp Nou days, the Spanish forward began to fluctuate and went eight games without scoring, ending the drought against Nice.

Industry observers note that maghnes Akliouche, bought from Monaco for £42.5m (€50m), has not yet reached his full potential (two goals and three assists in 16 matches), which is normal for a newcomer. But the lack of prior experience as a protagonist in the Champions League raises doubts over whether the 24-year-old Frenchman is able to make a difference for PSG.

It is a similar case to Mika Godts, acquired from Ajax for £46.8m (€55m), but with the aggravating factor that he is still going through the process of adapting to French football. As he is still 21, the Belgian winger has been inconsistent at PSG, with two goals and two assists in 12 matches.

Finally, Senny Mayulu (20) and Quentin Ndjantou (19) are academy gems still looking to establish themselves among the professionals. The Spanish manager does have the possibility of pushing Nuno Mendes and/or Achraf Hakimi forward, but that would create a problem at full-back.

PSG have seven more games until the winter break, but with Ligue 1, the Coupe de France and the Intercontinental Cup, it is undeniable that the mission of chasing a third successive Champions League title has become much harder without Doue.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hundreds of millions of people around the world are affected by diabetes mellitus1. It develops when the activity of insulin, a glucose-lowering hormone secreted by pancreatic β-cells, becomes insufficient to maintain healthy glucose levels in the blood. The condition can be managed with oral medication or by injecting insulin and other metabolic hormones, but the constant need for people with diabetes to manage their lifestyle and blood-glucose levels can impair their quality of life. Therapeutic approaches that monitor and control blood glucose automatically are therefore highly desirable. Writing in Nature, Xiu et al.2 report proof of principle of a bioelectronic device called NeuroAxis that does exactly that in rat models of diabetes.

AC Milan boss Ruben Amorim has ruled out the potential signing of Sporting CP defender Goncalo Inacio in January.

Amorim coached Inacio during his tenure at Sporting from March 2020 to November 2024, with the defender progressing through the club's youth ranks.

Inacio played 123 Primeira Liga matches under Amorim's tutelage, winning the league title in 2020-21 and in 2023-24, though the Portuguese coach left midway through the latter victory to join Manchester United.

Among Sporting defenders during Amorim's reign, Inacio ranked second for tackles won (94), interceptions (140), duels won (460) and aerial duels won (219) in the league, coming in behind Sebastian Coates in all four categories.

Sporting are third in the Primeira Liga this season, but have won three of their four Champions League games (L1).

Inacio has been linked with a move to Milan in January to reunite with Amorim, but the latter has denied the rumours.

"No, that is not true. Goncalo will not arrive," Amorim told Sport TV, as quoted by O Jogo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of vital saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

It has been revealed that alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Industry observers note that zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

Sources indicate that “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

According to recent reports, “We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

Recent findings suggest that it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

In a recent development, mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”.

Emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

But the Spaniard mentioned: “For different reasons, not only rest.”.

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

According to recent reports, tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

Sources indicate that “If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

In a recent development, “It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.
